column1: The history of the world’s most luxurious fabric, from ancient China to the present day
column2: 从古代中国到今天，回顾世界上最华贵的织物的历史。

column1: Silk is a fine, smooth material produced from the cocoons — soft protective shells — that are made by mulberry silkworms (insect larvae).
column2: 丝是一种纤细光滑的材料，取自桑蚕结出的茧。桑蚕是昆虫的幼体，茧是它们柔软的保护壳。

column1: Legend has it that it was Lei Tzu, wife of the Yellow Emperor, ruler of China in about 3000 BC, who discovered silkworms.
column2: 传说发现蚕的人是嫘祖，她是黄帝的妻子。黄帝约在公元前3000年统治中国。

column1: One account of the story goes that as she was taking a walk in her husband’s gardens, she discovered that silkworms were responsible for the destruction of several mulberry trees.
column2: 按其中一种说法，嫘祖在丈夫的园子里散步时，发现几棵桑树遭到破坏，而祸首正是蚕。

column1: She collected a number of cocoons and sat down to have a rest.
column2: 她拾起一些蚕茧，坐下来歇息。

column1: It just so happened that while she was sipping some tea, one of the cocoons that she had collected landed in the hot tea and started to unravel into a fine thread.
column2: 碰巧她喝茶时，刚捡到的一个蚕茧掉进了热茶里，开始解开，抽出一根细丝。
column3: It just so happened|事情恰巧是这样

column1: Lei Tzu found that she could wind this thread around her fingers.
column2: 嫘祖发现，她可以把这根丝缠在手指上。

column1: Subsequently, she persuaded her husband to allow her to rear silkworms on a grove of mulberry trees.
column2: 后来，她说服丈夫，让她在一片桑树林里养蚕。
column6: a grove of mulberry trees|一片桑树林

column1: She also devised a special reel to draw the fibres from the cocoon into a single thread so that they would be strong enough to be woven into fabric.
column2: 她还发明了一种特殊的缫丝器，把蚕茧中的纤维抽出并合成一根丝线，使它足够结实，可以织布。

column1: While it is unknown just how much of this is true, it is certainly known that silk cultivation has existed in China for several millennia.
column2: 虽然传说有几分属实尚不清楚，但有一点可以肯定：中国栽桑养蚕的历史已有数千年。

column1: Originally, silkworm farming was solely restricted to women, and it was they who were responsible for the growing, harvesting and weaving.
column2: 最初，养蚕完全是女性的工作，养殖、收获和织造均由她们负责。

column1: Silk quickly grew into a symbol of status, and originally, only royalty were entitled to have clothes made of silk.
column2: 丝绸很快成了身份的象征。起初，只有王室成员有资格穿丝绸衣服。

column1: The rules were gradually relaxed over the years until finally during the Qing Dynasty (1644-1911 AD), even peasants, the lowest caste, were also entitled to wear silk.
column2: 随着岁月流逝，这些规定逐渐放宽。到了清朝（公元1644—1911年），就连处于最低社会阶层的农民也有权穿丝绸。

column1: Sometime during the Han Dynasty (206 BC-220 AD), silk was so prized that it was also used as a unit of currency.
column2: 汉代（公元前206年—公元220年）的某段时期，丝绸极受珍视，甚至还被当作货币单位。
column3: Sometime during|在……期间的某个时候
column6: a unit of currency|货币单位

column1: Government officials were paid their salary in silk, and farmers paid their taxes in grain and silk.
column2: 官员以丝绸领取俸禄，农民则以粮食和丝绸缴税。

column1: Silk was also used as diplomatic gifts by the emperor.
column2: 皇帝还把丝绸当作外交礼物赠予他方。

column1: Fishing lines, bowstrings, musical instruments and paper were all made using silk.
column2: 钓线、弓弦、乐器和纸都曾用丝制作。

column1: The earliest indication of silk paper being used was discovered in the tomb of a noble who is estimated to have died around 168 AD.
column2: 最早表明丝纸已被使用的证据，发现于一位贵族的墓中。据推算，此人约死于公元168年。

column1: Demand for this exotic fabric eventually created the lucrative trade route now known as the Silk Road, taking silk westward and bringing gold, silver and wool to the East.
column2: 人们对这种异域织物的需求，最终催生了今天所称的丝绸之路。这条利润丰厚的商路将丝绸运往西方，又将金、银和羊毛带回东方。
column5: lucrative trade route|利润丰厚的商路

column1: It was named the Silk Road after its most precious commodity, which was considered to be worth more than gold.
column2: 这条路以沿途最珍贵的商品丝绸命名，当时人们认为丝绸甚至比黄金还值钱。

column1: The Silk Road stretched over 6,000 kilometres from Eastern China to the Mediterranean Sea, following the Great Wall of China, climbing the Pamir mountain range, crossing modern-day Afghanistan and going on to the Middle East, with a major trading market in Damascus.
column2: 丝绸之路从中国东部直达地中海，全长超过6000公里；它沿长城向前，翻越帕米尔山脉，穿过今天的阿富汗，继续通往中东，而大马士革就是沿途的一个重要贸易市场。
column5: Great Wall of China|中国长城
column9: major trading market|重要贸易市场

column1: From there, the merchandise was shipped across the Mediterranean Sea.
column2: 货物从那里装船，运过地中海。

column1: Few merchants travelled the entire route; goods were handled mostly by a series of middlemen.
column2: 很少有商人走完全程，大部分货物是经由一连串中间商转手的。
column6: a series of middlemen|一连串中间商

column1: With the mulberry silkworm being native to China, the country was the world’s sole producer of silk for many hundreds of years.
column2: 因为桑蚕原产于中国，数百年间，中国一直是世界上唯一的丝绸生产国。
column6: many hundreds of years|好几百年

column1: The secret of silk-making eventually reached the rest of the world via the Byzantine Empire, which ruled over the Mediterranean region of southern Europe, North Africa and the Middle East during the period 330-1453 AD.
column2: 制丝的秘密最终经拜占庭帝国传到世界其他地方。公元330—1453年间，这个帝国统治着南欧、北非和中东一带的地中海地区。
column4: rest of the world|世界其他地方

column1: According to another legend, monks working for the Byzantine emperor Justinian smuggled silkworm eggs to Constantinople (Istanbul in modern-day Turkey) in 550 AD, concealed inside hollow bamboo walking canes.
column2: 据另一个传说，有些僧人为拜占庭皇帝查士丁尼办事。他们在公元550年将蚕卵藏在中空的竹制手杖里，偷偷运到君士坦丁堡（今土耳其伊斯坦布尔）。
column9: hollow bamboo walking canes|中空的竹制手杖

column1: The Byzantines were as secretive as the Chinese, however, and for many centuries the weaving and trading of silk fabric was a strict imperial monopoly.
column2: 不过，拜占庭人和中国人一样严守秘密，丝绸的织造与贸易连续数百年都由皇室严格专营。

column1: Then in the seventh century, the Arabs conquered Persia, capturing their magnificent silks in the process.
column2: 7世纪，阿拉伯人征服波斯，在此过程中也获得了当地华美的丝绸。

column1: Silk production thus spread through Africa, Sicily and Spain as the Arabs swept through these lands.
column2: 于是，随着阿拉伯人席卷这些地方，丝绸生产也传遍非洲、西西里和西班牙。

column1: Andalusia in southern Spain was Europe’s main silk-producing centre in the tenth century.
column2: 10世纪，西班牙南部的安达卢西亚是欧洲主要的丝绸生产中心。

column1: By the thirteenth century, however, Italy had become Europe’s leader in silk production and export.
column2: 但到了13世纪，意大利已在欧洲的丝绸生产和出口中居于首位。
column3: By the thirteenth century|到十三世纪时

column1: Venetian merchants traded extensively in silk and encouraged silk growers to settle in Italy.
column2: 威尼斯商人广泛开展丝绸贸易，并鼓励蚕农到意大利定居。

column1: Even now, silk processed in the province of Como in northern Italy enjoys an esteemed reputation.
column2: 直到今天，在意大利北部科莫省加工的丝绸仍享有盛誉。

column1: The nineteenth century and industrialisation saw the downfall of the European silk industry.
column2: 进入19世纪，随着工业化的发展，欧洲丝绸业走向衰落。

column1: Cheaper Japanese silk, trade in which was greatly facilitated by the opening of the Suez Canal, was one of the many factors driving the trend.
column2: 推动这一趋势的因素有很多，其中之一是较为便宜的日本丝绸，苏伊士运河的开通让这种丝绸的贸易方便了许多。
column7: driving the trend|推动这一趋势

column1: Then in the twentieth century, new manmade fibres, such as nylon, started to be used in what had traditionally been silk products, such as stockings and parachutes.
column2: 到了20世纪，尼龙等新型人造纤维开始用于制造长袜和降落伞等产品，而这些东西传统上都用丝来做。

column1: The two world wars, which interrupted the supply of raw material from Japan, also stifled the European silk industry.
column2: 两次世界大战打断了日本原料的供应，也压制了欧洲丝绸业的发展。
column5: supply of raw material|原料供应

column1: After the Second World War, Japan’s silk production was restored, with improved production and quality of raw silk.
column2: 第二次世界大战后，日本恢复了丝绸生产，生丝的产量和质量都有所提高。
column3: Second World War|第二次世界大战

column1: Japan was to remain the world’s biggest producer of raw silk, and practically the only major exporter of raw silk, until the 1970s.
column2: 直到20世纪70年代，日本一直是全球最大的生丝生产国，也几乎是唯一的主要生丝出口国。
column7: until the 1970s|直到二十世纪七十年代

column1: However, in more recent decades, China has gradually recaptured its position as the world’s biggest producer and exporter of raw silk and silk yarn.
column2: 不过，近几十年来，中国逐渐重新成为世界最大的生丝和丝纱生产国、出口国。
column3: in more recent decades|在近几十年里
column4: recaptured its position|重新取得地位
column5: producer and exporter|生产国和出口国

column1: Today, around 125,000 metric tons of silk are produced in the world, and almost two thirds of that production takes place in China.
column2: 如今，全球丝产量约为12.5万公吨，其中将近三分之二产自中国。
column5: almost two thirds|将近三分之二
